text:
Cutter Gauthier scored three times, and Anaheim erased a three-goal deficit to beat Ottawa 6-3 at Honda Center. Gauthier, the fifth pick in the 2022 draft by Philadelphia, got his hat trick in a stretch of 36 seconds' worth of third-period power-play goals, the second and third coming 1:50 and 2:26 into the period. Judd Caulfield added two goals and an assist, and Roger McQueen finished it with a power-play goal in the third.

Ottawa had the early game. The Senators scored three times in the first period, including Philip Tomasino's snap shot at 6:00 and Claude Giroux's at 7:02, and held a 1.15 to 0.38 edge in expected goals (a measure of chance quality) for the period. After that the game turned. Anaheim outchanced Ottawa in the second and third, and by the end the teams were nearly level in total chance quality, 2.93 for OTT and 2.86 for ANA. Our simulation of every shot gave Ottawa a slight edge, 52 percent to 48 percent, in how often each side deserved to win.

The difference was the power play. Anaheim scored on four of its five chances, worth 1.34 expected goals, while Ottawa went 0 for 3 and took 25 penalty minutes to Anaheim's 12. In goal, Jonas Johansson allowed about three goals more than the 33 shots he faced should have produced, while Laurent Brossoit stopped 19 of 22.

The data doesn't give streaks or standings for either club, but the Ducks leave with a comeback from three goals down, and Ottawa with a game it controlled early and could not hold.
